candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — IV magnesium in torsades de pointes
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate treatment of long-QT torsades from other polymorphic ventricular tachycardia: defibrillate sustained polymorphic VT promptly and consider magnesium for recurrent torsades associated with long QT.

options.A: Routine magnesium is recommended for every episode of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, including episodes with a normal QT interval.
options.B: Magnesium replaces immediate unsynchronized shock when sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is present.
options.C: Magnesium may be considered to suppress recurrences of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with a long QT interval (torsades de pointes).
options.D: Magnesium is contraindicated in torsades de pointes because it predictably worsens QT-related ventricular instability.

candidate.rationale: The 2025 AHA Adult Advanced Life Support guideline states that immediate unsynchronized shock is recommended for sustained polymorphic VT. For recurrences associated with a long QT interval (torsades de pointes), magnesium may be considered. Routine magnesium is not recommended for polymorphic VT with a normal QT interval. Therefore C is correct; A overgeneralizes magnesium use, B incorrectly substitutes medication for required defibrillation of sustained polymorphic VT, and D reverses the guideline recommendation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sustained polymorphic VT requires immediate unsynchronized shock; magnesium may be considered for recurrent long-QT polymorphic VT/torsades, but routine magnesium is not recommended when QT is normal.
candidate.source_document_title: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support — 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
